issues.description: Resolver.resolve() postcondition silently weakened: returned requirements may no longer be fully prepared.
issues.detail: The resolver previously guaranteed every requirement had prepared=True and needs_more_preparation=False. That block was deleted without updating the documented contract. The obligation is now scattered across install/download/wheel, so any other caller (extensions, future commands, tests) inherits a half-prepared set. State the new postcondition explicitly on Resolver.resolve().

issues.description: set_dist/get_dist cache can return a stale metadata-only distribution after full preparation.
issues.detail: _fetch_metadata_only stores a metadata-only BaseDistribution in self._distribution. get_dist() returns it in preference to metadata_directory and local_file_path, so once the full wheel is later downloaded the cached metadata-only dist still wins. Invalidate _distribution on full preparation, or document last-writer-wins and enforce equivalence.

issues.description: set_dist/get_dist introduced with no documented preconditions, postconditions, or invariants.
issues.detail: set_dist accepts any BaseDistribution with no docstring, no idempotency contract, and no statement about when callers may use the cached value. For a mutable cache touched by resolver, preparer, and installer, the spec is the contract. At minimum: document that it stores a metadata-only view, may be superseded, and define what happens on repeated calls.

issues.description: prepare_linked_requirements_more call copy-pasted across three commands instead of a shared helper.
issues.detail: download.py, install.py, and wheel.py each independently call preparer.prepare_linked_requirements_more on the resolved set. A fourth command (e.g., lock) will forget. Push the step back into resolve() behind a dry_run flag, or introduce one finalize_resolution helper that owns the invariant.

issues.description: download_info populated via direct_url_from_link with no documented precedence and unclear behavior when source_dir is unset.
issues.detail: _fetch_metadata_only unconditionally fills download_info with direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir) when None. In dry-run, source_dir may be missing, hashes are absent, and pip lock/--report now consume values that differ subtly from the full-download path. Document the contract and test dry-run + VCS + --report explicitly.

issues.description: No test demonstrating that --dry-run actually avoids the wheel download.
issues.detail: The headline behavior is 'dry-run no longer downloads full wheels,' but the diff includes no test that fails on the old code and passes on the new. Add a functional test against a PEP-658 metadata path asserting wheel bytes are not fetched, so the regression cannot return silently.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the intent — moving eager preparation out of resolve() so dry-run and lock can skip wheel downloads — is correct and overdue. The unanimous objection is at the contract level: Resolver.resolve()'s postcondition was silently weakened, and the new obligation was sprinkled across three commands rather than centralized. The set_dist/get_dist cache is the most concrete correctness risk, since it can return a stale metadata-only distribution after a full download lands. Specs for set_dist/get_dist and download_info population are missing, and the headline behavior ships without a regression test. NEEDS-WORK: document contracts, invalidate the cache on full prep, consolidate the call site, and add the dry-run test.
